messages:
Alex Chen: hitting SSL errors when using the async python client against Private with a custom CA + http proxy. works fine with curl but sdk fails with aiohttp cert verify error

Maria Gomez: ugh, can you paste the traceback and your client init?

Alex Chen: stack: 
```\nTraceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 42, in <module>
    await client.chat.generate(...)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 123, in _request
    raise ssl.SSLCertVerificationError("certificate verify failed")
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed: unknown ca
```
Client init: 
```\nfrom redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://private.redwood.internal", proxy="http://proxy.local:3128")
```
I tried setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE on the runner, but sdk still fails.

Samir Patel: are you running inside the dev docker image? our image sets REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE but aiohttp doesn't automatically pick that up unless trust_env is True and you use TCPConnector from aiohttp.

Kevin Li: another gotcha: aiohttp's ssl handling needs an SSLContext passed to the connector if you want a custom CA file. env vars affect requests (sync) not always aiohttp (async).

Maria Gomez: quick workaround: create ssl.SSLContext and pass it into AsyncClient if client exposes connector/ssl_context. Example: 
```\nimport ssl
from redwood import AsyncClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="/etc/ssl/private-ca.pem")
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://private.redwood.internal", proxy="http://proxy.local:3128", ssl_context=ctx)
```
That made it work for me locally.

Alex Chen: thanks, that works locally. but two issues: 1) the typed AsyncClient signature doesn't include ssl_context in stubs — mypy complains. 2) onboarding docs don't show this, so most users will hit the opaque ssl.SSLCertVerificationError and copy-paste insecure workarounds like verify=False.

Samir Patel: agreed. filing an action: add explicit ca_bundle / ssl_context kwarg to AsyncClient constructor, update typing and docstrings, and improve error message when verify fails to surface "did you use a private CA or proxy? see redwood.dev/ssl".

Kevin Li: for Dedicated/Private we also need to ensure base_url normalization doesn't strip port or add trailing slash which broke our internal proxy health checks in an earlier release. tiny bug but painful.

Maria Gomez: also request: support trust_env flag (default True for sync, but defaults differ today in our async client). unify defaults across SDKs. add it to typing so it's discoverable.

infra-bot: created issue #3421: "py-async: support ca_bundle/ssl_context + trust_env parity + clearer SSL error" assigned to @Samir. CI label applied. :gear:

Samir Patel: I'll take it. Plan: add optional ca_bundle: str | None and ssl_context: ssl.SSLContext | None to AsyncClient, update __init__ typing, wire through aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_context, enable_cleanup_closed=True), and add test using a local proxy + custom CA in infra tests.

Alex Chen: awesome. can you also add a short example to quickstart showing the ssl_context workaround and env var notes? saves hours of debugging for new customers.

Samir Patel: yep will include sample snippet and a short troubleshooting section. tagging @Maria for docs review.

Maria Gomez: happy to review. also let's add a tiny lint rule to catch public client signatures that are missing typed kwargs compared to sync client. Caught a few regressions already.

Alex Chen: thanks all. leaving the workaround in place for now, will switch to new param once released. :thumbsup:
